title: 8 Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) Solutions: Our Top Picks by Use Case (2026)
content_md: Bottom line up front: EDR software generates work. Before choosing a platform, answer one question honestly who will look at the alerts, and when? If the answer is “nobody after 6pm,” buy a managed service or a platform that responds on its own. If you have analysts, buy for telemetry depth. Those two answers point to completely different products. EDR continuously records endpoint activity, detects attacker behaviour that prevention missed, and gives you tools to investigate and contain it. Stage 1 — Decide Whether You Need EDR or Something Else Work through this before looking at a single vendor. Your situation What you actually need No one monitors security alerts Managed detection and response, not EDR Someone checks a console during office hours EDR with strong automated response Small security team, no 24/7 rota EDR with autonomous containment, plus MDR overnight Full SOC with analysts EDR with deep telemetry and flexible hunting Compliance requires endpoint detection evidence EDR at a tier with adequate retention Cloud and container workloads dominate EDR with genuine Linux and container coverage Budget is the binding constraint Microsoft Defender if you hold E5, or an open-source approach The uncomfortable truth: an EDR platform nobody monitors is an expensive audit log. It records what happened, which helps after the fact, but it does not protect you.
